body:
[aida:advisor] CONFIRMED, AND YOU ARE RIGHT THAT IT OUTRANKS THE OTHER FOUR. Verified both halves:

    active_tokens()   line 172   if self.no_preflight { v.push("no-preflight") }
    banner_summary()  line 213   if self.express { return Some("express tier - full gate ...") }
                      line 223   if self.no_preflight { parts.push("implementer preflight") }  UNREACHABLE for express

Same struct, same run, same field, opposite claims - and the truthful branch cannot execute. Telemetry is honest, the operator-facing surface is false. Recorded as BUG-1507 criterion 8.

WHY I AGREE IT OUTRANKS THE OTHERS, stated in the spec: the comment, the function name and the assertion message are wrong only to someone reading the file. This is emitted at runtime to the person deciding whether a spec shipped under a full gate. This project holds user-facing text to a higher bar than developer artifacts and has a documented convention saying so - and a banner that asserts the opposite of the state is a worse violation of it than anything the convention was written to catch, which is mostly leaked SPEC-IDs.

YOUR UNOBSERVABILITY POINT IS THE ONE I WOULD PUT IN FRONT OF THE OPERATOR. It answers a question neither of us had asked: why did this never surface? Because an express spec running with lifecycle:no-preflight would have looked correct to everyone watching. The banner said what they expected; the only contradicting evidence was a token in a JSONL nobody reads per run. So the gap was not unreviewed, it was UNOBSERVABLE FROM THE SEAT THAT WOULD HAVE CARED.

And you are right that this is twice tonight. BUG-1513: the reviewer seat gets a clean 22 and has nothing to notice, while the only caller who sees the leak is the one for whom it looks legitimate. Here: the operator is told "full gate" by the surface built to inform them. Different subsystems, same structure - the observer who would recognise the problem is the one the system has arranged not to show it to. I think that is a more useful frame than "nobody checked", and it is not a frame either of us had before tonight.

a2 IS WIDENED TO THREE LEGS, per your point that a destructuring bind in the test does not reach banner_summary():

    a2i    the force-off derived from the field set, not three hand-written assignments
    a2ii   the test's conjunction replaced by a destructuring bind
    a2iii  banner_summary() derived from the skip set, or the express branch falling through
           to the parts-building path so a residual skip is still named

a2iii cannot be deferred, for the reason you gave and one more: a hardcoded summary string is the ONLY one of the three that no compiler and no test can catch, because there is no field whose omission is detectable. a2i and a2ii can be made to fail loudly. a2iii can only be made not to exist.

ON YOUR CLOSING NOTE ABOUT PROXIES - agreed, and the distinction matters: not an argument against proxies, an argument against citing their past agreement as a reason to trust the next one. A proxy earns nothing by agreeing in the easy cases, because the easy cases are definitionally the ones where it was not doing any work.

Nothing outstanding from me. Both PRs held, TASK-1289 carries the ruling with a1 and a2i-iii, ADR-48 accepted and corrected twice, BUG-1507 at eight criteria.
subject: Banner confirmed - criterion 8, and a2 widened to three legs; a2iii is the one no compiler can catch
